Rights: instrument_rights_register.csv row 'BIS/BAS scales, Carver & White (1994)' verdict=ship (Ben 2026-09-23, irw#2381 R02). Processing script data/goldberg_2018_escs.py.
note: mapping_basis=data_labels, no inference in the code->text tie: data/goldberg_2018_escs.py melts PRS.tab with var_name='item' and renames nothing; BLOCK_NAMES[('prs','pr')]='bas_bis' routes the pr* family here, so live codes pr1..pr20 ARE the .tab column names (core model s3 pattern 1). Tie to text: the DDI <labl> of each pr variable, 20/20 labelled. Three-way check: DDI labels = PRS_items.txt lines 316-335 = PRS.pdf p.10 statements top to bottom, 20/20 in order and identical after normalising punctuation/case. Corroboration (not required for data_labels; no export, irw_table_sets per_item): DDI valid-N equals live per-item n 20/20 (723-735; total 14,640 rows) and DDI min/max equals live resp_min/resp_max 20/20, including the only two items with no 1 responses (pr7, pr15, min 2). text_source=study_materials: item_text is the printed form wording (pdftotext -layout of p.10, checked against a 110-dpi page render). Deviations from the DDI labels, all typographic: the form's sentence-final periods are kept (the DDI/txt omit them); the form's curly apostrophes/quotes (pr7 'I’m', pr10 '“no holds barred”', pr11 '“worked up.”', pr12 'I’m') are shipped as printed where the DDI carries U+FFFD replacement characters; DDI trailing spaces (pr10, pr20) stripped; pr17's line-wrap joined with a space. Content: these are the 20 scored Carver & White (1994) BIS/BAS items (BIS 7, BAS Drive 4, Fun Seeking 4, Reward Responsiveness 5) in Goldberg's own order, without the 4 filler items; wording is the study's, which differs slightly from the canonical form in places (e.g. pr5 lacks the canonical 'important' at the end: '...done poorly at something.'). Shipped as administered, not normalised to canonical. instructions = the section's two-sentence paragraph verbatim (underline on 'you' dropped); instrument composes the booklet title, the section heading 'Personal Reactions' and the instrument attribution (the attribution is from the register/technical report, not printed on the form). option_text from the scale box: 1 Strong Disagreement, 2 Disagreement, 3 Agreement, 4 Strong Agreement (the box prints 'Strong' and 'Disagreement'/'Agreement' on two lines, joined with a space); the DDI has no value labels and the script stores the .tab integers unchanged, so resp = bubble number. Reverse-keyed BIS items pr17 (mean 2.03) and pr19 (2.49) are stored raw, not reversed. Rights: register verdict ship applied, not re-derived -- Carver's instruments page: 'All of these scales are being made available here for use in research and teaching applications. All are available without charge and without any need for permission.'

Philipp, 2025, 'Länder Expert Survey (LES) 2025: Hamburg', Harvard Dataverse V1, doi:10.7910/DVN/VFTK3K (CC0 1.0): codebook_EN_hh.pdf (file 10949322, sha256 ce9e0016f83e8ed0ac07a1c403135d8bccfc5ee957f52841f92e06d6dee5112c) and les_expert_level_long_hh.csv (file 10949320, sha256 98e8a6f3a718a48e7ba5fd2ce4b1b1c70779ec16dfd4835fea628d487fe02325); processing script data/thomeczek2025_les.py. Scratch under itemtext/.cache/thomeczek2025_les/.
note: ITEM AXIS: data/thomeczek2025_les.py melts the deposit CSV's columns by name with no rename (code IS the source column name, core model s3 pattern 1). The CSV carries no labels; the deposit's English codebook prints each question under a heading that is exactly the column name (leftrightgeneral, lrecon, ... publicbroadcast), so mapping_basis=paper_explicit (label match, codes also self-describing), 20/20. 'missiles' is in the script's list and the CSV header but has 0 non-missing cells in the Hamburg file and no codebook entry, so it is absent from the live table and from this file. Row reconciliation: melting the 20 columns of les_expert_level_long_hh.csv and dropping NA gives 3,661 rows = live row count (205 party-by-expert rows, 16 experts, bl hh and 1nat). TEXT: item_text is the codebook question with its trailing parenthetical pole labels removed; option_text is the two pole labels, 1 and 20, exactly as printed ('(1: ..., 20: ...)'); resp 2-19 are unlabelled in the source and left blank (the codebook: 'The content variables were surveyed on a scale of 1 to 20 ... labeling of the poles of the rating scale'). Every item_text and pole label was checked as an exact substring of the whitespace-normalised pdftotext output, 20/20 and 40/40. Line wraps joined; 'post-\nmaterialist' joined as 'post-materialist' (hyphen kept); curly quotes around 'debt brake' and 'Mietpreisbremse' kept; source wording kept as printed including 'over which federal state have legislative powers', 'the abolition ‘Mietpreisbremse’' and 'has been proven itself'. No respondent-facing instructions are printed, so instructions is blank. LANGUAGE: text_source=translated_substitute, language=German, translation_source=study_supplied. The respondents were German political-science experts rating German state parties, and the same author's later deposit 'Länder Expert Survey und Party-Check 2026' (doi:10.7910/DVN/NSPGMQ) carries codebook_de_26_bwrp.docx (sha256 bebdc887e9dfe0f8a9e545473d7699d81d18785ea2c2ea968d843baa66d15963), titled 'Länder Expert Survey (LES) 2024-2026', which says it 'enthält die exakten Fragentexte' and whose item table marks hh_2025 for every item here -- so the administration was German and the English codebook is the author's rendering. The German wording is not in this deposit (4 files: codebook_EN_hh.pdf, long/wide/median CSVs, no German text) and was deliberately NOT shipped from the sibling deposit: it is off-source, and it is not a reliable record of the 2025 Hamburg wording -- its assimilation item reverses the poles (1 'Für kulturelle Vielfalt', 20 'Anpassung von Migrant/-innen') whereas the Hamburg English codebook has 1 assimilation / 20 multiculturalism, and the Hamburg data follow the English (AfD mean 1.25, Greens 17.14). A later backfill of German wording would have to settle per item which wave's German matches the 2025 poles. VERIFICATION (option axis): AfD-minus-Greens means have the sign implied by the shipped pole labels on all 20 items (|diff| 5.7-16.1), and FDP-minus-Linke on the 4 economic items (|diff| 12.1-17.0); see verify_thomeczek2025_les.R. RIGHTS: the questions are the LES author's own (lrecon and galtan adapt Chapel Hill Expert Survey wording, as the galtan text itself says); deposit CC0 1.0; no restriction statement from the author or on the codebook located, so nothing to quote -- silence. Not in instrument_rights_register.csv. DATA NOTES (not item text): the codebook lists Freie Wähler (fw) among parties but the data hold Volt (volt) and no fw; the codebook states n_answered max 20 in one place and max 21 in another.
public_note: The Hamburg LES was administered to German experts in German; the item text shown is the author's English codebook, and the German wording is not in this deposit.
